record.paper_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
record.original_question: For integrable nonlinear partial differential equation systems, whose solution spaces have infinitely many degrees of freedom, are the currently known infinitely many symmetries complete, or do additional undiscovered symmetries exist beyond the standard families already generated in the literature?

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 2: Completeness of known infinitely many symmetries
For nonlinear physical systems with finite n freedoms described by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) system, it suffices to identify a finite number of symmetries or conserved quantities, as the general solution of the model possesses a finite number of arbitrary constants. However, for systems with infinitely many freedoms described by partial differential equation (PDE) systems, assessing the completeness of their symmetries is exceedingly challenging.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u=u(x,t,\ldots)$ denote the dependent variable(s) of an integrable nonlinear partial differential equation (PDE) system

$$ u_t = K(u, u_x, u_{xx}, \ldots), $$

whose solution space is infinite-dimensional. A symmetry of the system is a vector field $\sigma$ in the space of dependent variables (possibly depending on $u$ and its derivatives, and on $x, t$) such that the linearized flow $u_\tau = \sigma$ commutes with the evolution $u_t = K$, i.e. $[K,\sigma] = 0$ in the sense of evolutionary vector fields. For typical integrable systems (such as the KdV, mKdV, nonlinear Schrödinger, sine-Gordon, KP, and related hierarchies), one knows several standard infinite families of symmetries, for instance:

(i) the commuting hierarchy of higher symmetries generated by a recursion operator $\Phi$ from a seed symmetry (e.g. $\sigma_n = \Phi^n K$),

(ii) the $K$-symmetries / master symmetries and Lie point/contact symmetries generating Galilean, scaling, and translation invariances,

(iii) $\tau$-symmetries obtained by combining master symmetries with the hierarchy.

Question. For a given integrable PDE system with infinitely many degrees of freedom, is the collection of all such standard, currently known infinite families of symmetries complete, in the sense that every (smooth, local, or appropriately defined nonlocal) symmetry of the system is a linear combination — with coefficients that may depend on $x$, $t$ and arbitrary functions — of the symmetries in these known families? Equivalently, characterize the full Lie algebra of symmetries of the system and determine whether it strictly contains the algebra generated by the known families, or whether the two coincide.
artifact.status_search_result: The completeness of the known infinite families of symmetries for integrable PDE systems is widely regarded as an open problem; while complete classifications exist for restricted classes (e.g. local generalized symmetries of certain scalar evolution equations via the symbolic method of Mikhailov–Shabat–Sokolov), the general question — especially when nonlocal symmetries are allowed — remains unresolved.
